identity.name: Neetu Yoshi Limited
identity.industry: Railways / Rolling-Stock Critical Components (castings, forgings & machined sub-assemblies for wagons, coaches & track)

summary.oneLiner: Neetu Yoshi is a small, debt-free, high-margin (~25% PAT) maker of RDSO-approved Class-A critical railway castings/forgings (wagon/bogie components) that delivered on its IPO commitments — FY26 total income INR 101 cr (+44% YoY) and PAT ~INR 25 cr (+53%) — and is now forward-integrating into complete bogies, track crossings/turnouts and coach components. The new IPO-funded plant commissions production from June 2026; management reiterates FY27 revenue guidance of INR 210–220 cr at ~25% PAT, scaling to a ~INR 340–350 cr peak by FY28 once both plants run full, with optionality into mining, thermal-power components and exports.

one-line thesis: Neetu Yoshi is a small, debt-free, high-margin (~25% PAT) maker of RDSO-approved Class-A critical railway castings/forgings (wagon/bogie components) that delivered on its IPO commitments — FY26 total income INR 101 cr (+44% YoY) and PAT ~INR 25 cr (+53%) — and is now forward-integrating into complete bogies, track crossings/turnouts and coach components. The new IPO-funded plant commissions production from June 2026; management reiterates FY27 revenue guidance of INR 210–220 cr at ~25% PAT, scaling to a ~INR 340–350 cr peak by FY28 once both plants run full, with optionality into mining, thermal-power components and exports.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | FY26 (full year) | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | INR 101 cr | +44% | SME; H2/FY26 call (half-year + FY) |
| PAT | ~INR 25 cr | +53% | "Committed to investors"; PAT margin ~25% |
| PAT margin | ~25% | maintained | Sustained via Price Variation Clause (PVC) on RM + entry-barrier pricing power |
| Tax rate | 17.5% (15% + 2.5% cess) | — | Concessional 115BAB regime (incorporated 2020, prod. before 2024); lifetime, no sunset |
| Cash flow | Positive | — | Debt-free; cash-generative |
| Order book | INR 140–150 cr (executable in FY27) | — | Mix: ~40% coach, ~20–30% track, rest wagon; ~40% direct govt, ~60% private |
| Receivables | ~INR 32 cr at 31-Mar → ~INR 20 cr as of call | spiked Mar | Seasonal: Railways' Feb–Mar funds exhausted, replenished April (half collected by Apr-15) |
| Other income | Up sharply | up | Interest on IPO FDRs |
| CWIP | INR 38 cr at Mar (now utilized) | — | New plant commissioned; ~80% paid, balance post-commissioning |
> One-offs / context: the other-income jump is IPO-FDR interest (not operating). Receivables look inflated at 31-Mar purely due to the Railways' fiscal-year-end fund cycle — normalizes in April.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue:** FY27 INR 210–220 cr (new plant ~INR 100–110 cr + old plant ~INR 110 cr). Peak/FY28 ~INR 340–350 cr (old ~INR 110–130 cr + new ~INR 200 cr + track ~INR 60–70 cr).
- **Margin:** ~25% PAT maintained ("bottom line is the prime target"); upside possible once new plant scales and on richer mix (complete bogies, track).
- **Seasonality:** FY27 H2 > H1 (new-plant production starts June → 2–3 months already lost in H1; H2 "linear rapid growth").
- **Track section:** currently ~INR 20 cr revenue (sub-assembly only) → INR 60–70 cr in two years once full turnout/crossing line scales.
- **New-plant production:** starts within June 2026 (other product lines); RDSO approval for the new plant expected "next month" (then direct-to-Railways tendering + extra margin).
- **Capex:** FY27 mostly harvesting prior-year capex; next capex = rubber & spring assembly line (precision), funded from internal accruals. Wagon manufacturing facility targeted ~3 years out (200 wagons/yr target).
- **Exports:** targeting first exports by FY28 (US/UK) once precision quality is sufficient.
order book & pipeline:
- Order book INR 140–150 cr (incl. open orders), executable within FY27. Composition: ~40% coach, ~20–30% track, balance wagon. ~40% direct from government (Railways), ~60% private.
- Demand driver: the "1 lakh wagon" national order wave (referenced as a ~INR 40,000 cr tender) reviving the wagon industry after a slowdown → flows to bogie & component makers (sub-assemblies + bogie orders come to component suppliers).
- ~25 RDSO-certified products today; 15–20 more in pipeline (3–7 month approval windows each), spanning wagon, coach and track. Applying not only to RDSO but to ICF, MCF, RCF (coach factories) and locomotive/track agencies.
- Channels: Railways via IREPS e-procurement; private via direct liaisoning. Customers/peers named: Jupiter, Titagarh and various track/coach companies (private but must buy from approved sources).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Old plant (<100 kg products):** existing RDSO-approved components; ~INR 110 cr revenue base.
- **New plant (IPO-funded, ~INR 50 cr capex; products up to 1 ton):** complete bogies + coupler + crossing + other lines; ~INR 100–110 cr target. RDSO approval pending (expected next month); meanwhile starts on already-approved product lines.
- **Track section:** scrap-based components cost ~INR 37–39/kg vs rail (bought from Jindal) at ~INR 65–70/kg requiring ~2 months inventory → higher working capital but higher margin. Sub-assembly now (~INR 20 cr), full turnout/crossing later.
- **Coach components:** ~40% of current order book; supplying via ICF/MCF/RCF approvals; Vande Bharat & coach upgradation a tailwind.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Mining components** — fungible assets, can manufacture without new capex.
- **Thermal-power / energy components** — government energy/thermal-generation push; existing plant can make these (no new capex).
- **Leasing & maintenance of railway lines** — new RDSO criterion; product+service (conditioning wagons, maintenance lines).
- **Complete assembly line ("merger of all criticality")** — cast/machined + fabrication (done) + rubber & spring plant (developing) → full sub-assembly to Railways.
- **Wagon manufacturing** — ~3 years out (200 wagons/yr).
- **Exports** — US/UK by FY28.
margins & cost dynamics:
- ~25% PAT sustained despite RM (steel/scrap, rail) inflation via Price Variation Clause (PVC) on government tenders + matching escalation understanding with private buyers (a "chain of reaction" as peers face same input costs).
- Lag exists product-to-product; defended by continuously rotating into newer/better-margin products as older ones see margin erosion from new entrants.
- Cost discipline: debt-free (no interest cost), location & tax benefits, focus on power/RM/interest cost reduction → margins above (unlisted) competitors.
- Bogie pricing fell from ~INR 3.25 lakh to ~INR 2.70–2.80 lakh during the wagon-industry slowdown; expected to recover as the 1-lakh-wagon order rolls out.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Prior-year ("seeds sown"): bogie plant (~INR 50 cr of the ~INR 77 cr IPO raise), track section, fabrication line. ~INR 10 cr residual bogie-plant capex completed in FY26.
- FY27: primarily harvesting (revenue generation from completed capex); next capex = rubber & spring assembly line, from internal accruals.
- Land available at the plant for brownfield expansion (site chosen for headroom).
- Watch: RDSO approval timing for new plant (gates direct-Railways tendering & extra margin); track-section working-capital ramp.
capital allocation:
- Debt-free; capex funded by IPO proceeds + internal accruals.
- ~INR 29 cr raised via warrants / preferential issue for the track section's working capital (rail inventory cost) — to be utilized over ~1.5–2 years; promoters also subscribed (to avoid diluting their holding). Minority dilution challenged by an investor; mgmt defended on cost-minimisation grounds (avoid debt/interest cost).
- No further dilution foreseen for working capital this year; future capex from internal accruals.
risks & watch-items:
- **SME-scale & key-man risk:** single promoter (Himanshu Lohia) is MD + CFO + sole call voice; family-run.
- **RDSO/ICF/MCF/RCF approval timing:** revenue & margin uplift gated by certifications (3–7 months each; new-plant approval still pending).
- **Receivable seasonality / Railways fund cycle:** debtors spike at FY-end (Feb–Mar) on Railways budget exhaustion.
- **RM inflation lag:** PVC mitigates but with product-level lag; bogie price compression during slowdowns.
- **Customer concentration:** Indian Railways + a handful of private wagon/coach/track OEMs; demand tied to national wagon-order cycle.
- **Working-capital intensity rising** in the track section (rail inventory ~2 months at INR 65–70/kg).
- **Guidance dependence on wagon-cycle revival** (1-lakh-wagon order materialising) and West-Bengal wagon-cluster regime change.
- **Dilution via warrants** for working capital (minority concern).
management quality / tone: - Confident, consistent and delivery-credible — multiple participants noted Neetu Yoshi is "one of the few SME companies consistent with guidance and achieved it." MD candid on margins, tax benefit and the receivable cycle. Promotional on long-dated optionality (mining, thermal, exports, wagon manufacturing) and somewhat vague on exact bifurcations (order-book split given as ranges). Audio/answer quality patchy on some questions. Reiterated bottom-line focus over topline.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The real moat is the RDSO/Class-A critical-component approval barrier: each product line has only 4–7 active suppliers, most unlisted (named: Frontera, Roys Steel, Atul Engineering — all private) — hence sustained ~25% PAT in a "boring" components business.
- The concessional 17.5% tax rate (115BAB-type, lifetime, no sunset) is a structural ~7.5 ppt margin edge vs 25%-payers — durable but non-replicable for new entrants who missed the 2020-incorporation / pre-2024-production window.
- This is a picks-and-shovels supplier to the listed wagon/coach OEMs (Jupiter Wagons, Titagarh, Texmaco) rather than a competitor — it sells components/bogies into them; the 1-lakh-wagon cycle lifts the whole stack.
- Track/turnout integration is the higher-margin but working-capital-heavy next leg (rail from Jindal); the ~INR 29 cr warrant raise is specifically to fund that inventory, not growth capex.
- Forward integration into complete bogies (new plant, <1 ton) is the FY27 swing factor — but it is RDSO-approval-gated; until then the plant runs on already-approved lines.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Old plant (<100 kg products):** existing RDSO-approved components; ~INR 110 cr revenue base.
- **New plant (IPO-funded, ~INR 50 cr capex; products up to 1 ton):** complete bogies + coupler + crossing + other lines; ~INR 100–110 cr target. RDSO approval pending (expected next month); meanwhile starts on already-approved product lines.
- **Track section:** scrap-based components cost ~INR 37–39/kg vs rail (bought from Jindal) at ~INR 65–70/kg requiring ~2 months inventory → higher working capital but higher margin. Sub-assembly now (~INR 20 cr), full turnout/crossing later.
- **Coach components:** ~40% of current order book; supplying via ICF/MCF/RCF approvals; Vande Bharat & coach upgradation a tailwind.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Order book INR 140–150 cr (incl. open orders), executable within FY27. Composition: ~40% coach, ~20–30% track, balance wagon. ~40% direct from government (Railways), ~60% private.
- Demand driver: the "1 lakh wagon" national order wave (referenced as a ~INR 40,000 cr tender) reviving the wagon industry after a slowdown → flows to bogie & component makers (sub-assemblies + bogie orders come to component suppliers).
- ~25 RDSO-certified products today; 15–20 more in pipeline (3–7 month approval windows each), spanning wagon, coach and track. Applying not only to RDSO but to ICF, MCF, RCF (coach factories) and locomotive/track agencies.
- Channels: Railways via IREPS e-procurement; private via direct liaisoning. Customers/peers named: Jupiter, Titagarh and various track/coach companies (private but must buy from approved sources).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue:** FY27 INR 210–220 cr (new plant ~INR 100–110 cr + old plant ~INR 110 cr). Peak/FY28 ~INR 340–350 cr (old ~INR 110–130 cr + new ~INR 200 cr + track ~INR 60–70 cr).
- **Margin:** ~25% PAT maintained ("bottom line is the prime target"); upside possible once new plant scales and on richer mix (complete bogies, track).
- **Seasonality:** FY27 H2 > H1 (new-plant production starts June → 2–3 months already lost in H1; H2 "linear rapid growth").
- **Track section:** currently ~INR 20 cr revenue (sub-assembly only) → INR 60–70 cr in two years once full turnout/crossing line scales.
- **New-plant production:** starts within June 2026 (other product lines); RDSO approval for the new plant expected "next month" (then direct-to-Railways tendering + extra margin).
- **Capex:** FY27 mostly harvesting prior-year capex; next capex = rubber & spring assembly line (precision), funded from internal accruals. Wagon manufacturing facility targeted ~3 years out (200 wagons/yr target).
- **Exports:** targeting first exports by FY28 (US/UK) once precision quality is sufficient.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Mining components** — fungible assets, can manufacture without new capex.
- **Thermal-power / energy components** — government energy/thermal-generation push; existing plant can make these (no new capex).
- **Leasing & maintenance of railway lines** — new RDSO criterion; product+service (conditioning wagons, maintenance lines).
- **Complete assembly line ("merger of all criticality")** — cast/machined + fabrication (done) + rubber & spring plant (developing) → full sub-assembly to Railways.
- **Wagon manufacturing** — ~3 years out (200 wagons/yr).
- **Exports** — US/UK by FY28.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- ~25% PAT sustained despite RM (steel/scrap, rail) inflation via Price Variation Clause (PVC) on government tenders + matching escalation understanding with private buyers (a "chain of reaction" as peers face same input costs).
- Lag exists product-to-product; defended by continuously rotating into newer/better-margin products as older ones see margin erosion from new entrants.
- Cost discipline: debt-free (no interest cost), location & tax benefits, focus on power/RM/interest cost reduction → margins above (unlisted) competitors.
- Bogie pricing fell from ~INR 3.25 lakh to ~INR 2.70–2.80 lakh during the wagon-industry slowdown; expected to recover as the 1-lakh-wagon order rolls out.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Debt-free; capex funded by IPO proceeds + internal accruals.
- ~INR 29 cr raised via warrants / preferential issue for the track section's working capital (rail inventory cost) — to be utilized over ~1.5–2 years; promoters also subscribed (to avoid diluting their holding). Minority dilution challenged by an investor; mgmt defended on cost-minimisation grounds (avoid debt/interest cost).
- No further dilution foreseen for working capital this year; future capex from internal accruals.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - Confident, consistent and delivery-credible — multiple participants noted Neetu Yoshi is "one of the few SME companies consistent with guidance and achieved it." MD candid on margins, tax benefit and the receivable cycle. Promotional on long-dated optionality (mining, thermal, exports, wagon manufacturing) and somewhat vague on exact bifurcations (order-book split given as ranges). Audio/answer quality patchy on some questions. Reiterated bottom-line focus over topline.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **SME-scale & key-man risk:** single promoter (Himanshu Lohia) is MD + CFO + sole call voice; family-run.
- **RDSO/ICF/MCF/RCF approval timing:** revenue & margin uplift gated by certifications (3–7 months each; new-plant approval still pending).
- **Receivable seasonality / Railways fund cycle:** debtors spike at FY-end (Feb–Mar) on Railways budget exhaustion.
- **RM inflation lag:** PVC mitigates but with product-level lag; bogie price compression during slowdowns.
- **Customer concentration:** Indian Railways + a handful of private wagon/coach/track OEMs; demand tied to national wagon-order cycle.
- **Working-capital intensity rising** in the track section (rail inventory ~2 months at INR 65–70/kg).
- **Guidance dependence on wagon-cycle revival** (1-lakh-wagon order materialising) and West-Bengal wagon-cluster regime change.
- **Dilution via warrants** for working capital (minority concern).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The real moat is the RDSO/Class-A critical-component approval barrier: each product line has only 4–7 active suppliers, most unlisted (named: Frontera, Roys Steel, Atul Engineering — all private) — hence sustained ~25% PAT in a "boring" components business.
- The concessional 17.5% tax rate (115BAB-type, lifetime, no sunset) is a structural ~7.5 ppt margin edge vs 25%-payers — durable but non-replicable for new entrants who missed the 2020-incorporation / pre-2024-production window.
- This is a picks-and-shovels supplier to the listed wagon/coach OEMs (Jupiter Wagons, Titagarh, Texmaco) rather than a competitor — it sells components/bogies into them; the 1-lakh-wagon cycle lifts the whole stack.
- Track/turnout integration is the higher-margin but working-capital-heavy next leg (rail from Jindal); the ~INR 29 cr warrant raise is specifically to fund that inventory, not growth capex.
- Forward integration into complete bogies (new plant, <1 ton) is the FY27 swing factor — but it is RDSO-approval-gated; until then the plant runs on already-approved lines.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4/H2 FY26 (this):** FY26 total income INR 101 cr (+44% YoY), PAT ~INR 25 cr (+53%, ~25% margin), debt-free, positive cash flow; order book INR 140–150 cr (executable FY27); 25 RDSO products + 15–20 in pipeline; new IPO-funded bogie/sub-assembly plant commissions production June 2026 (RDSO approval pending ~next month); ~INR 29 cr warrant/pref raise for track-section working capital. FY27 guidance reiterated INR 210–220 cr at ~25% PAT; FY28 peak ~INR 340–350 cr; exports targeted FY28; full wagon manufacturing ~3 yrs out.
- _Next H/Q → check: (1) new-plant RDSO approval received? (2) new-plant production actually started June + H2>H1 ramp; (3) FY27 revenue tracking to INR 210–220 cr at 25% PAT; (4) track section scaling toward INR 60–70 cr; (5) receivables normalising off the Mar spike; (6) 1-lakh-wagon order flowing into order book; (7) warrant proceeds deployment; (8) rubber & spring assembly-line capex._
